status_reasoning: Reviewers accept the DNA binding data showing KDM2B recognizes non-methylated CpG islands through its ZF-CxxC domain. No concerns were raised about the EMSA or ChIP-seq data demonstrating this specific recognition, indicating implicit acceptance of these foundational findings.

Reviewers request clarification on 'What PRC1 protein(s) does KDM2B interact with? With what protein domain? Why does it not recruit CBX-containing complexes?' This indicates the interaction data is accepted but the mechanistic details and specificity require better explanation in the text.

Reviewers ask 'What excludes KDM2A from Polycomb target CGIs?' indicating they accept the observation that KDM2B is enriched at polycomb sites while KDM2A is depleted, but want better explanation of the underlying mechanism for this differential localization.

Reviewers note 'Only a small subset of KDM2B binding sites are also occupied by RING1B so other features or factors must be involved in the recruitment of PRC1.' They accept the widespread RING1B binding data but question why KDM2B presence alone is insufficient for robust PRC1 recruitment at most sites.

Reviewers question 'why, if KDM2B is required for all Ring1b binding sites, loss of KDM2B only derepresses a very small subset.' This highlights a logical inconsistency between the widespread role of KDM2B in RING1B recruitment and the limited gene expression changes upon KDM2B depletion.

Reviewers state 'The loss of H2Aub even from those genes that are supposed to be derepressed after KDM2B knockdown is not impressive: in most cases it is no more than 20% lower. That means that the 40% loss in global H2Aub is not concentrated in these genes and suggests that KDM2B plays a minor role in recruiting some kind of PRC1.' This directly challenges the claim that KDM2B-mediated recruitment is functionally important at derepressed genes.

The modest locus-specific H2AK119ub1 loss at derepressed genes (noted by reviewers as 'not impressive') raises questions about whether KDM2B recruitment truly 'contributes to' H2AK119ub1 and gene repression in a functionally significant way, though the data show some effect.

Reviewers note 'nothing was said about recruitment of CBX-containing PRC1. Evidently these are not recruited by KDM2B. So there are several links missing in the causal chain.' They accept that KDM2B recruits a variant PRC1 complex but want clarification on how this relates to canonical CBX-containing PRC1 and the overall model.

Reviewers ask 'How is PRC2 recruited to KDM2B/RING1B sites? It seems to be there according to Figure 2... Is a CBX protein associated with these sites? Is there H3K27me3 associated with KDM2B/RING1B binding sites?' They accept the spatial correlation data but want mechanistic explanation for PRC2 co-localization.

Reviewers ask 'What are H3K36 demethylases doing at sites not expected to contain H3K36 methylation?' This questions the functional relevance of KDM2A/B demethylase activity at CGIs, though they don't dispute the targeting data itself.

Reviewers state 'Without a mechanism to recruit PRC2 to the same sites, the model is not very explanatory' and note 'several links missing in the causal chain.' While they accept the core finding that KDM2B links PRC1 to CGIs, they find the overall model incomplete without explaining PRC2 recruitment and CBX-PRC1 targeting.

Reviewers explicitly criticize 'the misguided insistence on the assumption that binding PRC1 automatically compacts chromatin, although in ES cells it is clear that many binding sites are the typical bivalent sites that also have methylated H3K4 and bind RNA polymerase.' This directly challenges the claim about chromatin compaction.
The reviewers do not question the immunofluorescence data showing KDM2B nuclear localization. This technical observation appears accepted without comment.

Reviewers do not challenge the data showing KDM2B binding depends on its ZF-CxxC domain and is independent of RING1B. These mechanistic findings establishing the direction of recruitment are implicitly accepted.

Reviewers ask 'Is this recruitment mechanism typical or is it specific for ESC cells?' regarding the widespread low-level PRC1 at CGIs. They accept the observation but question its generality and the 'sampling' interpretation, wanting clarification on cell-type specificity.
Reviewers do not question the knockdown validation data showing specific KDM2B depletion without affecting other polycomb proteins. These technical controls are implicitly accepted.
Reviewers do not challenge the observation that KDM2B knockdown does not globally affect H3K27me3 or H3K4me3. This finding is implicitly accepted as it helps define the specificity of KDM2B's role.
